objects.original: The finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E; its centered standard Gaussian γ; the exact unit-sphere subtype S; a joint probability law P on E×ℝ with Gaussian first marginal and L² response; polynomial p; arbitrary parameter probabilities μ,ν; the literal predictor f_μ, potential V_μ, actual ambient gradient g_μ, projected vector G_μ, angular cost c and all-coupling value Q.
objects.reconstructed: Finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space E with its Borel structure; true joint probability P with actual standard-Gaussian first marginal; real polynomial p; actual response coordinate; unit subtype S; arbitrary parameter measures; actual integral predictor and scalar potential V; totalized ambient gradient grad; projected formula G; concrete angular cost c; extended squared-cost coupling infimum Q; and uniform positive output constants C1,C2.

domains.original: E is a real finite-dimensional inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure. P is a probability measure on E×ℝ. The parameter laws are probability measures on S={w:‖w‖=1}. Predictor inputs and weights in the potential/gradient existence assertion range over all E. Tangency, norm and joint law/point estimates range over exact unit points. Q takes values in ℝ≥0∞; its half-power is converted to ℝ only after finiteness is proved.
domains.reconstructed: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures; completeness follows from finite dimensionality. P:Measure(E times R) is a probability with P.map Prod.fst=stdGaussian(E). p:Polynomial R. Response membership is in real Lp R 2 P. S={w:E | norm(w)=1} inherits its structures. predictor:Measure S->E->R; V:Measure S->E->R; grad,G:Measure S->E->E; c:S times S->R; Q:Measure S->Measure S->nonnegative_extended_reals. Predictor integrals use the parameter measure on S, potential integrals use P on E times R, and transport lower integrals use coupling measures on S times S.

quantifiers.original: For every fixed E,P,p satisfying the Gaussian first-marginal and response-L² conditions, there exist C₁,C₂>0 before all μ,ν,w,u. For every probability μ: the potential cross term is integrable and the actual gradient exists at every ambient w; tangency and the C₁ bound hold for every unit w. For every probability pair μ,ν: Q is finite, and the C₂ estimate holds for all unit w,u.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every E and its structures, joint probability P with its actual Gaussian first-marginal equality, polynomial p, and supplied response L2 witness, let S,predictor,V,grad,G,c,Q be fixed by their formulas. There exist strictly positive C1,C2:R before all subsequent universal quantifiers. The first block quantifies every mu:Measure S with probability; for every ambient w:E it concludes cross-term integrability and genuine HasGradientAt, and for every w:S it concludes orthogonality and the C1 norm bound. The second block quantifies every pair mu,nu:Measure S with both probability; it concludes Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and then the single C2 estimate for every w,u:S. No per-law or per-point choice of constants occurs.

assumptions.original: E is finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel; P is a probability with P.map fst = stdGaussian E; p is a real polynomial; the actual response (x,y)↦y belongs to L²(P). The subsequent analytic claims have probability premises on μ and ν. No input/response independence, derivative witness, domination estimate, feature mean bound, integral identity or gradient oracle is a premise. Completeness of E is derived. The six reader conditions correctly include definitions and conclusions rather than treating Q finiteness or constants as extra assumptions.
assumptions.reconstructed: The listed finite-dimensional real inner-product and Borel measurable-space structures, P being a true joint probability, the equality of its actual first marginal with stdGaussian(E), an arbitrary given real polynomial p, and genuine L2(P) membership of z->z.2. Laws in the universal conclusion must be probabilities. Cross-term integrability, actual ambient differentiability, uniform projected-vector bounds, cost finiteness, and law-plus-angle control are all conclusions, not supplied hypotheses. There is no product-law assumption, independence, explicit feature derivative input, supplied norm constant, finite-support restriction, or cost-finiteness premise.

conclusion.original: For every parameter probability and ambient weight, the literal potential cross integrand is integrable and HasGradientAt holds for its actual Mathlib gradient. On unit weights G is tangent and uniformly bounded by C₁. For every probability pair, Q<∞ and ‖G_μ(w)-G_ν(u)‖≤C₂(sqrt(Q)+arccos(inner(w,u))). The square root is the real value of the extended square root after finiteness. No optimal coupling or intrinsic geometric identification is asserted.
conclusion.reconstructed: There exist C1,C2:R with C1>0 and C2>0, uniform for all subsequent laws and unit weights. For every probability mu on S, and every ambient w:E, the scalar function z->(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) is genuinely Bochner integrable under P, and HasGradientAt(V(mu,.),grad(mu,w),w) holds. For every such probability mu and every w:S, inner_product_E(w_bar,G(mu,w_bar))=0 and norm_E(G(mu,w_bar))<=C1. For every probability pair mu,nu on S, Q(mu,nu)!=infinity and, for all w,u:S, norm_E(G(mu,w_bar)-G(nu,u_bar))<=C2*((Q(mu,nu)^(1/2)).toReal+c(w,u)). Exact definitions and their totalizations: Let S={w:E | norm_E(w)=1} with its inherited topology and measurable structure, and denote the ambient representative of w:S by w_bar. For every mu:Measure S and x:E define predictor(mu,x)=integral_S p.eval(inner_product_E(w_bar,x)) dmu(w). Define V(mu,w)=2*integral_{E times R}(predictor(mu,z.1)-z.2)*p.eval(inner_product_E(w,z.1)) dP(z), for every ambient w:E. Define grad(mu,w)=gradient(V(mu,.),w), the actual Mathlib full ambient gradient, and G(mu,w)=grad(mu,w)-inner_product_E(grad(mu,w),w) times w. Define c(w,u)=Real.arccos(inner_product_E(w_bar,u_bar)) on S times S. Define Q(mu,nu) as the infimum in the nonnegative extended reals of integral_lower_{S times S} ofReal(c(w,u)^2) dgamma(w,u), over actual measures gamma whose first marginal is mu and second marginal is nu. The empty feasible infimum is infinity; no optimizer is selected or asserted. All predictor and potential integrals are actual real Bochner integrals, totalized to zero if their integrands fail to be integrable. The gradient definition is totalized at points without the corresponding Frechet derivative.

scopes.original: The predictor and scalar potential are literal Bochner integrals. Their analytic properties are proved for probability parameter laws, despite total definitions existing for all measures. Gradient differentiability is full ambient pointwise differentiability with μ fixed. A.e. class identities are used only as intermediate bridges; final scalar function/gradient assertions are pointwise in ambient weights. Projection and estimates are for unit points. If S is empty, probability-conditioned clauses are vacuous. This is a quantitative continuity/boundedness result, not a convergence theorem.
scopes.reconstructed: The Gaussian is the actual first marginal of the fixed joint law P, without an independent response replacement. For each probability mu the scalar cross-term integrability and ambient gradient are asserted for every w:E, including nonunit points; the only scalar function being differentiated is the explicit V(mu,.), with mu fixed. HasGradientAt certifies the actual Frechet derivative represented by the actual grad value, so under these conditions it does not rely on nondifferentiable totalization. G is a true orthogonal tangent projection only for norm(w)=1, and the orthogonality, norm bound, and final comparison are restricted to those subtype points. The definitions are syntactically available for all measures via totalized integrals and gradients, but no analytic conclusion is extended beyond their probability premises. The explicit Integrable clause concerns exactly the displayed joint cross integrand. Q is the nonnegative extended infimum of lower integrals over ordered-marginal couplings, not a signed measure operation. Q finiteness is explicit and prevents interpreting an infinite transport root by toReal=0. No optimizer or new metric/geodesic API conclusion is included. All parameter probabilities, including nonatomic ones, are covered. No law-variable derivative is asserted. Empty S is allowed, making the probability-conditioned assertions vacuous.

constant_dependencies.original: C₁,C₂ are real and strictly positive, chosen from the fixed E,p,P and response norm before every parameter-law and unit-point quantifier. They are independent of μ,ν,w,u. No dimension-free bound, explicit polynomial dependence or numerical rate is claimed.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: C1,C2 are existential finite reals with strict positivity, uniform over all subsequent probability laws and unit weights. They may depend on the fixed E,P,p and the response moment information already contained in the fixed data; no formula, optimality, or dimension/joint-law independence is specified. V has literal coefficient 2. G has exactly one copy of grad minus its normal component, without an additional outer factor. The cost is exactly c squared, with real exponent 1/2 on the extended transport value. The final estimate has one C2 multiplying the sum of the finite root transport value and c(w,u), without further normalization or a particle-count factor. No assumption that Q or G is strictly positive is imposed.

binders_and_definitions.typing: NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace, finite dimensionality and Borel measurable structure match E. CompleteSpace is derived, not an extra assumption.
binders_and_definitions.source_premises: P probability, exact first marginal, p polynomial, actual response MemLp2; probability premises on subsequent parameter laws.
binders_and_definitions.definitions: S is the literal unit-sphere subtype. predictor and V are actual Bochner integrals; actual integrability is proved under the probability premises. gradient is the Riesz representative of the total Fréchet derivative, and HasGradientAt establishes genuine differentiability. G is literal normal-component subtraction. transportCost is an extended nonnegative infimum over all measures with the specified marginals; probability marginals force coupling probability. The angular cost is arccos(inner), with no new metric installed.

module_audit.proof_assessment: The complete proof constructs the Gaussian derivative, pullback isometry, joint-L² feature, literal mean bridge, scalar potential identity and actual gradient; it then transfers the parent projected-gradient bounds. The target is more than a renamed parent conclusion because the literal joint-law potential and actual gradient bridges are discharged here.

steps.title: Differentiate the Gaussian feature in L2
steps.assessment: Actual Gaussian derivative producer supplies every-ambient-weight differentiability and positive operator bounds on the closed unit ball; no derivative witness enters the target binders.

steps.title: Pull the feature into the joint data space
steps.assessment: First-coordinate measure preservation constructs J. The proof composes derivatives and uses J.norm_map to preserve the operator bound and Lipschitz estimate. The reversed hLip arguments match its declared orientation.

steps.title: Identify the true parameter average
steps.assessment: Gaussian averaging supplies scalar integrability, Bochner integrability and exact L² mean identity. Pullback and ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm prove hMeanClass; coeFn_toLp and coeFn_sub give the needed a.e. predictor and residual identities.

steps.title: Recover the literal scalar potential
steps.assessment: L2.inner_def and integral_congr_ae give equality of ambient scalar functions. The residual and feature L² memberships imply product integrability; its explicit final construction appears in step 7 at module line 149.

steps.title: Differentiate and identify the actual gradient
steps.assessment: The quadratic feature-law parent applies to the proved F,DP bounds. hPot transports its HasGradientAt statement to the literal potential. Gradient uniqueness is made explicit by HasGradientAt.gradient in the adjacent hG block and final conclusion.

steps.title: Project onto tangent directions
steps.assessment: hG computes the exact normal-component subtraction from the actual gradient by HasGradientAt.gradient. For unit w, the parent supplies tangency and C₁ through the final step at module lines 153–155. No intrinsic manifold-gradient claim is made.

steps.title: Keep the angular cost and pass to joint law/point control
steps.assessment: The final conjunction explicitly returns potential integrability, actual-gradient existence, unit-point tangency/boundedness, Q≠∞ and the all-law/all-unit-point estimate. C₁,C₂ were obtained before the μ,ν introductions. The parent coupling definition and probability normalization support the source all-couplings interpretation.
